activities.title: A probability table must add to 1

assessmentPoints: Table sum answers in the probability table activity
successCriteria: I can check that 0.2 + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1, so the table for X = 0, 1, 2 is a valid distribution
I can find P(X = 2) = 1 - 0.2 - 0.5 = 0.3 when X = 2 is the only other outcome
objectives.text: Check a discrete probability distribution by summing its probabilities to 1

assessmentPoints: Expectation answers in the balance point activity
successCriteria: I can read expectation as the balance point and the long-run average over many repeats, even though X can never equal 1.1
objectives.text: Compute expectation as a probability-weighted average and read it as a balance point

assessmentPoints: Binomial answers in the binomial activity
Exit responses in the toolkit activity
successCriteria: I can choose the successful trials, then multiply by one path's probability
objectives.text: Use the binomial formula: choose the successful trials, then multiply by one path's probability

assessmentPoints: Trap answers in the toolkit activity
successCriteria: I can state that about 95% lies between 80 and 120 for a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 10
I can state that after five heads the next toss is still 1/2 heads, because the tosses are independent
objectives.text: Use the 68-95-99.7 rule for a normal distribution and state what independence means

subject: math
title: JC H2 probability: distributions, binomial, normal, independence
